title: PlacementNeed
description: A placement need: an intent to receive (spec §7.1, VF Intent with the receiver named), item S3. What kind of carrying, under which key, how many holders across how many failure domains, what a carrier must provide, the kind's terms, the reach it was expressed at (it crosses no wider, spec §7.2), the one receiver it is carried for, who expressed it, its serve-order class, and the space whose membrane it was expressed in. Its identity is content-derived: `Need::id` is the atom CID of the canonical DAG-CBOR encoding, the key explanations and carrying records join on (D10); a JSON form decoded and re-encoded to DAG-CBOR gives the same id as one built in Rust (G1 contract vector). A device's own needs never take this shape: they exist only as private needs on the device (R6). Sources: the app manifest's `needs` reader (§G), a person's keep intents, a TaskSpec (§F). Wire shape: this schema is the source of record; placement_core::Need (elohim/placement/core/src/need.rs; serde camelCase, deny_unknown_fields; every CID a string in JSON) is its Rust mirror, not yet pinned to it by a test (follow-on: a placement-core schema_contract case that validates one serialized Need per NeedTerms and NeedKey form here). The Rust codec is the authority only for the canonical DAG-CBOR bytes and `Need::id`. Source of truth: the need's source, from which it is derived each pass (Category C); it is never notarized itself; what is recorded is the carrier's commitment (Category A above public reach, household-local below, R2).

demand.title: Demand
demand.description: How many honored holders across how many distinct failure domains, resolved by the space's charter from the content type's declared loss (Charter::resolve). `domains` is at most `holders`; JSON Schema cannot compare the two, and the Rust constructor and the charter hold it.

domains.description: Distinct failure domains wanted among them.

requires.title: Requirements
requires.description: What a carrier must provide. Every field is always written; a null means the need sets no bound on that dimension (one provenance).

alwaysOn.description: Whether the carrier must be always on.

bytes.description: For a task: disk bytes plus the materialized view's size (F16). A u64 in Rust, bounded here to 9007199254740991 (2^53 - 1, the largest integer every JSON reader, JavaScript included, holds exactly); a larger value is refused, never rounded.

memoryBytes.description: A u64 in Rust, bounded here to 9007199254740991 (2^53 - 1, the largest integer every JSON reader, JavaScript included, holds exactly); a larger value is refused, never rounded.

isolation.description: The weakest isolation the need accepts (F6); null accepts any.

items.description: An agent key (`uhCAk…`), the canonical agent identity (elohim_epr_rea::model::AgentRef / AgentRefKey, a string newtype). Never a transport id and never a CID.

carriers.description: A narrowing every peer's admit sees (`--on`, F14): only these agents may carry. Null: any carrier. A set, sorted in the canonical encoding.

terms.title: NeedTerms
terms.description: Kind-specific terms inside the need's canonical encoding (F4), internally tagged by `terms`.

scope.description: The compute-grant scope derived one way from the method (F1), never written by the requester.

oneOf.description: A root the requester believes a berth holds, so only the delta is fetched (F9).

baseRoot.description: Null when the requester names no base root.

reach.description: The reach the need was expressed at; it crosses no wider. Below public, placement is household-local and not notarized (R2).

receiver.description: Carried for whom: one receiver per need. An agent key (`uhCAk…`), the canonical agent identity (elohim_epr_rea::model::AgentRef / AgentRefKey, a string newtype). Never a transport id and never a CID.

expressedBy.title: Expresser
expressedBy.description: Who expressed the need. A struct with a `by` field rather than an internally tagged enum, so the JSON and DAG-CBOR forms are both honest (G1). There is no device expresser.

id.description: The manifest or charter CID string, or the person's or agent's key.

inScopeOf.description: The space whose membrane the need was expressed in (VF in_scope_of), a CID string. The legacy custody scope is the raw-codec CID of the name elohim:placement:legacy-custody-scope@1.
